partial_progress.details: Phase 2 (unit selection and stack ordering) is [COMPLETED] and committed with full scoped verification, on top of the already-completed Phase 1. Phases 3-7 (the cut/manifest ref-writing, restack, handoff integration, /merge stack mode, redeploy + second-repository demonstration) remain -- each is substantial git-plumbing and test-fixture work. Closing here depth-first after one fully-verified phase rather than rushing the remaining five in the same dispatch.

artifacts.summary: Phase 2 completion state, key decisions (selection gather-vs-validate split, the 5 Phase-1 assertions repointed to show, the untested --order chain simplification, the untested pull-in refusal branch), and the Phase 3 starting point.

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented and fully verified Phase 2 of 7: review-stack-prepare.sh's cut now selects tasks (--milestone/--batch/--tasks), attributes each to a landing proof or a fallback commit-subject convention, merges shared_paths/--merge pairs into units, pulls in an unmerged path-overlapping earlier task, groups units into components over dependency edges and path overlap, orders each component topologically with an ancestry tie-break and a contradiction refusal, and assigns each unit a branch and a base -- printing the result, writing nothing. Suite grew from 19 to 28 cases, all passing; committed cleanly. Phases 3-7 remain for a follow-up dispatch.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan phase adds a new mandatory input (e.g. a required selection flag) to a subcommand whose earlier resolution stages an existing test suite already exercises with that input absent, split the new requirement into a non-refusing 'gather' step (runs early, so later resolvers that want the new input's value can use it when present) and a separate 'validate' step (refuses on absence, called only from the new feature's own body, after the pre-existing resolvers run). This keeps every pre-existing success/refusal assertion reachable unchanged instead of needing to retrofit a selection onto fixtures that were never about selection.

A simple bash union-find for grouping a small set of string/number keys (e.g. task numbers merging into review units): two associative-array functions, uf_find (recursive, path-compressing, lazily initializing UF_PARENT[x]=x on first touch) and uf_union (union the two roots), called as plain statements since bash functions return values via stdout capture, which this pattern avoids on the hot path by using a parent-pointer array instead.

To generate genuine 'observed failing before passing' evidence for a verification criterion after a feature was authored in one complete draft (rather than incrementally red-green), temporarily neutralize the specific guard function with a one-line sed substitution (e.g. replacing a call with ':' plus a comment), re-run the suite to confirm the targeted case fails for the expected reason, then restore the backup and re-run to confirm it passes again. Cheap, and keeps the verification claim honest rather than asserting a TDD sequence that did not actually happen.

sapience_notes.subject: cut subcommand selection resolution ordering for the stack-PR-submission task
sapience_notes.value: review-stack-prepare.sh's cut subcommand gathers its selection (--milestone/--batch/--tasks) before resolving the integration branch, review base, remote and platform, but only VALIDATES that selection (refusing when absent or empty) after those four resolvers run and inside cut's own body. The first draft validated immediately on gathering and broke every one of the prior phase's success/refusal assertions that call cut with no selection at all to exercise those shared resolvers.

sapience_notes.subject: git merge-base --is-ancestor as the landing-order comparator
sapience_notes.value: Two commits' chronological landing order on a linear branch is correctly compared with `git merge-base --is-ancestor A B` (true iff A happened before B on that branch), independent of commit timestamps; a test fixture that wants to control 'landing order' must control which stack_commit call runs first, not timestamp fields, since both commits can be made within the same second.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh OWED-NOT-PAID fallback recurring across two phases of the same task
sapience_notes.value: review-stack-prepare.sh and its suite remain unmapped by suite_selection_select even after a second phase of edits (0 suites selected, 2 owed, across 2 touched paths); the OWED-NOT-PAID fallback battery (98 suites) ran instead of a targeted set, and passed cleanly, matching the same shape the prior phase of this same task observed with a different fallback battery size (237 suites, when manifest.json/suite-classification.data were also touched).

sapience_notes.subject: branch slug for a merged review unit
sapience_notes.value: When two or more tasks merge into one review unit (via shared_paths or --merge), the unit's branch slug is taken from the lowest-numbered member task only, not a concatenation of every member's slug. Chosen to keep branch names bounded in length and because the plan's own wording names a single 'task slug', not a joined one.

sapience_notes.subject: untested paths in the stack-PR-submission task's unit-selection phase
sapience_notes.value: Two code paths in review-stack-prepare.sh's cut selection/ordering body have no suite case yet: the --order flag's single-chain override across multiple components, and the earlier-unmerged-task pull-in's refusal branch for an unselectable match (every landing-proof entry the scan finds is, by construction, resolvable, so only the pull-in path -- not the refusal path -- is currently reachable). Both are candidates for a case before a later phase relies on them.
